pageTitle: Set up custom planning rules with Klacksy | Klacks

hero.titleHtml: Your industry is not listed? Klacksy sets up your rules in dialogue.
hero.subtitle: Whether you start from an industry template or from scratch: Klacksy guides you through the setup one question at a time, explains the planning impact of every value, and applies nothing without your explicit confirmation.
hero.screenshotAlt: Klacksy guides you through the custom planning-rules setup in a Q&A dialogue

items.title: No industry template fits
items.text: Home care, security or logistics cover a lot — but your company agreement, your surcharges and your rest times are exactly yours.

items.title: Customizing without coding
items.text: Classic planning software demands consultants or scripts for custom rules. Here you simply describe your rules in your own words — Klacksy does the rest.

items.title: Rules must act inside planning
items.text: A rule in a PDF protects nobody. Only when the planner checks it on every shift assignment does it become real protection for your team.

steps.title: Three steps to your planning profile

items.title: Choose your starting point
items.text: Klacksy asks first: should an industry template be copied as your editable starting point — or do you start from scratch with a single blank rule?

items.title: Answer question by question
items.text: Klacksy asks for each parameter one at a time — working hours, caps, rest times, surcharges — explaining what the value means and how it changes the plan. Open required fields and values already collected are visible at any time.

items.title: Review the preview, then confirm
items.text: Before saving, Klacksy shows the complete rule set as a preview. Nothing is applied until you confirm — transactional, traceable in the rule register, and reversible.

solutions.title: What Klacksy asks about
solutions.subtitle: 16 parameters, each with its meaning and planning impact — these are the topic areas.

items.title: Working-time baseline
items.text: Standard daily hours and the weekly hours of a full-time workload — the reference for part-time percentages and target-hour calculations.

items.title: Caps
items.text: Maximum hours per day and per week — the planner refuses shifts that would exceed them.

items.title: Consecutive & rest days
items.text: How many working days in a row are allowed and how many rest days per planning window are guaranteed.

items.title: Rest breaks & night surcharge
items.text: Minimum rest between two shifts plus the start, end and rate of the night surcharge window.

items.title: Overtime
items.text: From how many hours worked time counts as overtime — accumulated per day or per week.

items.title: Holidays & vacation
items.text: The surcharge rate for working on public holidays and the annual vacation entitlement for staff on this rule.

example.title: A security company sets up its 12-hour rule
example.text: Starting point: the „Security“ industry template as a basis. Klacksy asks in sequence: „How many hours may a shift last at most?“ — answer: 12. „How many consecutive days are allowed?“ — 3. Every answer is explained with its planning impact, and finally the preview shows the entire profile. One click on confirm — and the rule applies to every automatic plan from now on.

cta.title: Set up your rules
cta.text: Start the dialogue with Klacksy in the playground — or install Klacks on your own infrastructure and define your planning rules in minutes instead of consultant days.
